course.title: Exoplanets and Astrobiology
course.description: Explores exoplanet detection, demographics, orbital architectures, atmospheres, biosignatures, habitable zone models, extremophiles, prebiotic chemistry, and the scientific limits of life detection.

status.reviewStatus: Approved for review release; not yet approved for instructional use

cadence.rationale: Matched 1:1 biweekly cadence, following the ASTR230/ASTR310/ASTR320/ASTR340 precedent (a 3-credit, 14-lecture structure), because ASTR350's seven thematic units are each exactly two lectures long (unlike ASTR320's variable 2-3 lecture units), so a strict two-lecture-per-lab grid is the natural, unambiguous cadence. See syllabus.html Lecture, Lab, and Problem-Set Cadence.

dataProvenance.src: materials/ASTR350/src/generate_astr350_content.py and generate_astr350_labs_psets.py generate all worked examples, lecture slides/notes, labs, and problem sets programmatically from shared constants.
realData: 51 Pegasi b and HD 209458 b system parameters - live-verified via direct web fetch this session (Wikipedia, 2026-09-24), citing Mayor & Queloz (1995) and Charbonneau et al. (2000)/Henry et al. (2000). A units error in the fetched 51 Pegasi b infobox (K given as km/s instead of m/s) was caught by cross-checking against the article's own prose and the published literature value, and corrected before use.

TRAPPIST-1 seven-planet system - reused and extended from this curriculum's ASTR320 course, where it was live-verified via direct web fetch (Wikipedia, 2026-09-24), citing Agol et al. (2021), Ducrot et al. (2020), Gillon et al. (2017), and Delrez et al. (2022). Per-planet mass/radius values are standard published (Agol et al. 2021), consistent with the range already established in ASTR320.

HD 80606 b and 16 Cygni B b (eccentric RV planets); extremophile survival/growth records; Miller-Urey relative amino-acid abundance ranking; Kasting-Whitmire-Reynolds (1993) habitable-zone flux boundaries - standard published primary literature, not independently re-verified this session, flagged for spot-check in reference-log.md.
Drake equation biological terms (f_l, f_i, f_c, L) - explicitly labeled illustrative/synthetic order-of-magnitude placeholders, not claimed measurements.
